name: LiveOpsPoppy
description: Your game's LiveOps backend in your own AWS — change balance, prices and features live without an app-store review, and see players, sessions and retention on a dashboard nobody else can read. No per-player fees, ever.

permissionSet.name: LiveOpsPoppy backend
permissionSet.description: Deploys and removes its own CloudFormation stack (named LiveOpsPoppyStack): one DynamoDB table, one collector Lambda behind a public URL, and a least-privilege execution role for that Lambda. Every change and delete is limited to resources named LiveOpsPoppy* (and a liveopspoppy-deploy-* code bucket) — it cannot touch anything else in your account. It creates one narrowly-scoped IAM role for its own Lambda; no account or organisation access. If you turn on the optional team dashboard it also creates a Cognito user pool for the people you invite: AWS generates that pool's id, so the create itself cannot be name-scoped, but every read, change and delete on a pool is restricted BY IAM to pools carrying LiveOpsPoppy's own tag — it can never list, empty or delete a user pool belonging to you or to another app. It also reads AWS's public price list (free, read-only, no data of yours involved) so the cost figures on the dashboard are AWS's real prices for your region rather than numbers baked into the app.

grants.reason: Looks up AWS's public price list so the dashboard can show what your setup actually costs. Public prices only — never your bill, your usage or your account.

grants.note: Creating the team viewer pool. A user pool's id is generated by AWS, so a create can never be scoped to a name that does not exist yet — this is the one Cognito grant that cannot be narrowed. It creates and describes only; nothing here can read a user, change a pool or delete anything. Tag/UntagResource are how CloudFormation applies the attribution tags (it tags in a SEPARATE call after create — CrewPoppy's live rollback, 2026-07-30).
grants.reason: Creates the sign-in directory for your dashboard. Changing or deleting a directory is a separate permission, limited to the one LiveOpsPoppy itself created.

grants.note: Managing that same pool and its viewer accounts — enforced by IAM to pools carrying LiveOpsPoppy's own tag, so no other poppy's user pool (a mail poppy's mailboxes, say) can be listed, emptied or deleted. The pool is born tagged from the stack's AttrAccountId/AttrConnectionId parameters.
